task: Run one bounded instruction and return one answer, or unavailable with a short reason. Supply all context and paths; the worker shares your files and can write, but has no firm tools or conversation history. Coordinate writes and review the result as your own work. Use a unique request_id for each new attempt; identical retries join or replay the same answer. At most two tasks run concurrently by default; extra capacity may be unavailable.
mandate_guidance: Other roles search mandates to find who is responsible for particular work. Describe this role’s responsibilities using concrete terms colleagues are likely to search for. Include common alternative terms where useful, and make ownership boundaries explicit.
configuration_error: Operations cannot arrange this work: the firm's configuration does not allow it, and you cannot change it. This failure does not open an owner request. If this blocks progress, tell your manager what you need unless they already know. Set a reminder only when a future check could help and no reply or other wake is expected. Take up other work, or finish normally to pause with working memory intact. Hand off only when you need a fresh start or Operations requires it.
send: Send immutable mail. Recipients are plain role addresses (founder/playtest), exact employee IDs (e1), or the reserved addresses owner and runtime (Operations). Do not prefix them with @. Attach a file the reader should open, such as a report. Supply its absolute path under your drive. Use a short, meaningful, unique request_id label for each operation. Reuse it only for an identical retry.
reply: Reply into a message's conversation. add brings people in: the talk moves to the conversation of the larger set, which continues this one. summarize=true attaches a derived summary of this conversation to that introduction, so newcomers need not ask for context. Attach a file the reader should open, such as a report. Supply its absolute path under your drive.
peek: List waiting mail by conversation, with each conversation's waiting message IDs, senders and subjects. Claims nothing; follow a returned cursor for another page.
claim: Read waiting mail and remove it from pending: everything in one conversation (oldest first, as much as fits; the result says how many remain), or exact message_ids. Claim is not task completion.
dismiss: Set waiting mail aside unread: one conversation, as of your last peek, or exact message_ids.
clear: Set aside everything that was waiting at your last peek in this work period. Mail that arrived since is untouched.
messages: Read exact immutable messages by ID without changing inbox dispositions.
context: Summarize a conversation's recent messages, reaching back into the conversation it continues; the result is derived and leaves inbox dispositions unchanged.
set_reminder: Schedule a self-reminder at a future UTC epoch timestamp. Delivers ordinary Operations mail when execution is open; handoff(wait) saves notes but does not release your current slot until you finish this work period.
list_reminders: List your pending self-reminders without changing them.
cancel_reminder: Cancel your pending reminder; already delivered mail is preserved.
hire: Hire a direct report with your exact mandate. They start automatically; do not send a duplicate kickoff. Every role can code, build, research and test; any role can lease a station on the firm's Mac, if it has one, with mac_acquire when it needs a native macOS build, simulator or desktop session. Omit temporary_periods for durable employment; supply it for a bounded appointment. ${mandate_guidance}
renew_temporary: Add work periods to an exact direct report without changing identity, files or working memory.
promote: Make a temporary direct report permanent without replacing its identity or working memory.
get_role: Inspect a current address or exact employee identity, with paged public profile, current mandate, and its workspace path when it is in your reporting line. A returned continuation is for you in this work period.
find_roles: Search current colleagues' public profiles and current mandates. A returned continuation is for you in this work period.
org_tree: Browse the current organization; follow a returned cursor for more roles. A returned continuation is for you in this work period.
revise_mandate: Revise a direct report's mandate at its expected revision. ${mandate_guidance}
fire: Retire a direct report with no live descendants; preserve its records.
retry: Request another attempt for a held direct report using its exact employee identity and the recovery revision in the Operations notice.
handoff: Save notes for a fresh start: after this work period finishes, both next=continue and next=wait replace your conversation memory with fresh working memory. Files, mail and saved notes survive. Choose continue to request another work period, or wait for new input. To pause while retaining your current working memory, finish normally without calling handoff, unless Operations requires a handoff. Set clean_up only when the work in scratch and Docker is finished: before your next work period, stopped containers, dangling images and build cache are removed and scratch is emptied (tagged images and volumes stay). Leave it unset for a fresh start mid-task, and name anything in scratch the next period relies on in your notes. Identical retries apply within this period. Finish this work period after saving.
request_access: Ask for access to something that exists but is not yours yet. Pass kind, the resource, and a short purpose the owner will read. Kinds: network_host, resource a lower-case host name (api.example.com, or *.example.com for its subdomains; no scheme, port, path or IP address), which once granted is open to the whole firm; github_repository, resource organization/repository in the firm's organization, granted at once for a repository this firm created or one already granted to you, and otherwise decided by the owner. Returns granted at once when you already have access; otherwise pending with the owner's request_id and a cause, and the owner's answer arrives later as mail: take up other work, or finish normally to pause with working memory intact; set a reminder when it serves a real future check, and hand off only when you need a fresh start or Operations requires it. Asking again returns your open request. Refused with a reason: access_kind_unknown, access_resource_invalid, github_not_configured, github_unavailable (try again later), or access_denied (the owner declined this resource; the owner_note says why, so do not ask again). Use a short, unique request_id; reuse it only for an identical retry.
create_repository: Create a new private GitHub repository named <firm id>-<name> in the firm's organization and get write access to it. name uses lower-case letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.'; purpose is one sentence. Returns at once: granted with the repository and its clone_url, after which git and gh work in it; or pending with the owner's request_id and a cause (github_auto_create_off: this firm does not create repositories on its own; github_limit_reached), where the owner decides and the answer arrives later as mail: take up other work, or finish normally to pause with working memory intact; set a reminder when it serves a real future check, and hand off only when you need a fresh start or Operations requires it; or refused with a reason: github_name_taken, github_not_configured, github_unavailable (try again later) or access_denied (the owner declined; the owner_note says why). For a repository that already exists use request_access. Use a short, unique request_id; reuse it only for an identical retry.
mac_acquire: Lease your own account and desktop on the firm's Mac for this work period. Returns granted with the SSH host, port, user, key_path (a private key file in your credentials directory), drive (the shared drive mounted on the Mac), project_dir (your workspace on it), scratch (the directory on the Mac to check out and build in), disk (the Mac's free space), disk_reclaimed (bytes cleared from the Mac before your lease began), and message with Mac workflow notes; busy when none can be granted and at least one is held, with the holders and since when; or unavailable with a reason, which includes the Mac being too full; or pending with the owner's request_id and a cause when only the owner can make the Mac ready (it is not set up, a desktop awaits verified cleanup, or no desktop account is ready), where the answer arrives later as mail: take up other work, or finish normally to pause with working memory intact; set a reminder when it serves a real future check, and hand off only when you need a fresh start or Operations requires it. Calling again while you hold it returns the same lease. Other roles may be working in their own accounts and desktops on the same Mac, so ports, CPU and Homebrew are shared and are not private. The drive is the shared store, not a working directory: check out from it into scratch, build there, and write deliverables back before you release. The drive's mount on the Mac has no atomic rename, so a parallel build on it fails on a different file each time. Keep nothing in your home on the Mac: release clears scratch, simulator devices, your temporary folder, Library caches, build products and what you added at the top of the home, but not the standard folders (Documents, Downloads, Desktop), which remain in your account. The Mac usually has Xcode with iOS and watchOS simulators, and Homebrew; check what is installed before relying on it. If Homebrew is installed, install what you need with brew; those installs persist and are shared. Release with mac_release when done.
mac_release: Release your Mac lease after saving work to the drive. Ends your SSH access, stops everything you started on the Mac (background processes, simulators, brew services and other LaunchAgents, crontab), closes helper apps and detaches the drive, then verifies all four. It also reclaims the Mac's disk: scratch, your simulator devices, your temporary folder, Library caches, logs, build products, the Trash and whatever else you added at the top of the home. It keeps Homebrew installs, apps in ~/Applications and the standard folders (Documents, Downloads, Desktop), so empty those yourself. Returns clean:true or the failed checks, plus disk (the Mac's free space) and disk_reclaimed (bytes your release cleared); end the remaining activity and call again if it was unclean.
mac_status: Report whether the firm has a Mac and, for each station on it, whether it is leased, by whom and since when, whether it awaits owner recovery, and which one you hold.
desktop_status: Check that the desktop tools are ready for your Mac lease. Requires holding the Mac (mac_acquire); otherwise returns reason=mac_not_held. Apps launched through the desktop tools run as the same Mac user as your SSH access, with the same drive at the lease's drive path.
desktop_apps: Requires holding the Mac. List applications launched through the desktop tools. Use returned process IDs with the other desktop tools.
desktop_windows: Requires holding the Mac. List windows belonging to a returned application process. Use returned window IDs with desktop_capture.
desktop_inspect: Requires holding the Mac. Inspect an application's accessible controls. Returns bounded elements, handles and supported actions. Reinspect when a handle becomes stale. Use desktop_capture and pointer tools for custom controls without accessibility handles.
desktop_launch: Requires holding the Mac. Launch an application by its absolute app bundle path. Returns its process ID for the other desktop tools. This operation is not automatically safe to retry.
desktop_action: Requires holding the Mac. Perform a supported accessibility action on a handle returned by desktop_inspect for the same application. This can change application data; inspect the result before retrying.
desktop_focus: Requires holding the Mac. Focus an accessible control using a handle returned by desktop_inspect for the same application.
desktop_type: Requires holding the Mac. Type up to 4096 UTF-8 bytes into an application. Supply a returned accessible handle to focus that control first, or use the existing focus. Oversized input returns reason=input_limit without sending text. Verify the target and result; retrying may enter duplicate text.
desktop_press_key: Requires holding the Mac. Press one macOS hardware key code (0–127) in an application launched through desktop_launch. Optional modifiers are command, shift, option and control. Common codes: A=0, S=1, L=37, Return=36, Tab=48, Space=49, Escape=53. Input targets only that tracked application, not other applications on the Mac. Shortcuts can change or save data; inspect the resulting window before retrying.
desktop_capture: Requires holding the Mac. Capture one returned window from an application. Returns the window image and capture details, and saves the image as a PNG in your workspace's captures/ directory: drive_path is the file relative to your drive, mac_path is the same file on the Mac. Reference drive_path in reports. If the save fails, save_message says so and the image is still returned.
desktop_click: Requires holding the Mac. Click within a captured window of an application launched through desktop_launch. Coordinates x and y are pixels measured from the screenshot's top-left corner. Choose left or right button. Optional modifiers are command, shift, option and control, held for the call; no application has yet been seen to honour a modifier on a pointer event, so use desktop_press_key for shortcuts. hold_ms (0–10000) is how long the button stays down between the press and the release, for a long press. This can change application data; capture the result before retrying.
desktop_drag: Requires holding the Mac. Drag with the left button within a captured window of an application launched through desktop_launch. Both endpoints are pixels measured from the screenshot's top-left corner. Optional modifiers are command, shift, option and control, held for the call; no application has yet been seen to honour one on a pointer event. hold_ms (0–10000) holds the button still at the starting point before the movement begins; duration_ms (50–10000) is how long the movement takes, and without it the drag uses its usual pacing. This can change application data; capture the result before retrying.
desktop_scroll: Requires holding the Mac. Send pixel scroll deltas at a point within a captured window of an application launched through desktop_launch. Coordinates x and y are pixels measured from the screenshot's top-left corner; delta_x and delta_y are signed integer scroll amounts. Optional modifiers are command, shift, option and control, held for the call; no application has yet been seen to honour one on a scroll. Capture afterward to verify how the target control responded before repeating.
desktop_tap_sequence: Requires holding the Mac. Post a planned passage of 1 to 64 taps within a captured window of an application launched through desktop_launch, as real pointer events on the same path as desktop_click. Each tap is x and y in pixels from the screenshot's top-left corner and after_ms (0–5000), the delay before it: from the start of the request for the first tap, from the previous tap for the rest. The delays together may not exceed 20000 ms; a longer passage is refused with reason=invalid_request and nothing is sent. Returns count and offsets_ms, the times the taps were actually posted at, so you can see how closely the passage was kept. You plan the whole passage in advance and see nothing between its taps: capture before and after, not during. Input targets only that tracked application, not other applications on the Mac. This can change application data; capture the result before retrying.
desktop_close_apps: Requires holding the Mac. Close applications launched through your desktop tools. Save application work to the drive first. This keeps your lease; mac_release ends it.
